clue.text: Wake-up call from Dorking, perhaps

parts.note: Dorking sounds like a town's alarm, but it is a breed of chicken, and a cockerel's crow is the farmyard wake-up call

explanation.surface: Someone in the Surrey town of Dorking is giving a morning alarm call.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorking is a Surrey town, but also an old English breed of domestic fowl; the 'call' is the crow of its rooster at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The conventional English rendering of a rooster's crow, heard at daybreak.

clue.text: Possible origin of stone could be obsolete

explanation.surface: A geologist wonders where a stone came from and what it might be.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading pictures a fruit stone, which could come from a date; the second is the everyday phrase for something superseded.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone could come from a date fruit, and a thing past its expiry is no longer current.

clue.text: Fighting with sticks has to ject

clue.text: Do countries make such gifts?

parts.note: countries is a plain synonym for nations

explanation.surface: A question about whether states hand out foreign aid.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: DO plus NATIONS, and countries do give such gifts as aid.
explanation.definitionFit: Gifts handed over to a cause or recipient are contributions of this kind.

clue.text: Lightweight showing a lot of resilience

indicators.note: a lot of, but not all, means the synonym loses one of its letters, here its first

parts.note: resilience, springiness, is bounce

explanation.surface: A small fighter shows great resilience in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lightweight' suggests a boxer, but it is the definition: a very small unit of weight. 'a lot of' drops the first letter of BOUNCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A small imperial unit of weight, about 28 grams, so a lightweight measure.

clue.text: Faithful bonds go to make Solution them

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Faithful bonds go to make Solution them (9)': 'Solution them' is OCR garble and the wordplay for LOYALTIES cannot be read; no search recovered the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Faithful bonds go to make Solution them

clue.text: Miserable returns after dramatic start turns to slump

indicators.note: after puts the returned piece behind the dramatic start in the answer
start means just the opening letter of the word dramatic
returns tells us the synonym for miserable is read backwards

parts.note: miserable in the sense of wretched or of low quality: poor

explanation.surface: A gloomy show-business story: a promising start turns into a slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miserable' looks like the definition, but slump is: 'turns to' is only a link, and 'returns' signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to sag or sink downward, as wilting flowers or tired shoulders do.

clue.text: Shops with expired leases

parts.note: expired, as a time or a fire that has run out, is out
lets are properties leased to tenants

explanation.surface: Retail premises whose rental agreements have lapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: Retail outlets are stores or points of sale.

clue.text: Top price offered for a house

definitions.text: Top price offered for a house

parts.words: Top price offered for a house
parts.note: top is a verb here: to outbid an agreed offer on a home after it has been accepted

explanation.surface: An estate agent records the highest bid on a property.
explanation.walkthrough: In British house-buying, a seller can accept a higher bid even after agreeing a sale; the verb for the rival buyer's trick is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A British term for outbidding a buyer whose offer had already been accepted on a property.

clue.text: Continue performing in the London area

explanation.surface: A performer keeps going in a part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: ACTON is a district of west London; split into two words it means carry on acting.
explanation.definitionFit: To act on is to keep acting, and Acton is a district of west London.

clue.text: Nurse gets turn at being Billy's partner

parts.note: a nanny is a children's nurse
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: A nurse finally gets her turn as a man called Billy's partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Billy' looks like a man's name but is a billy goat, a male goat.
explanation.definitionFit: A female goat is the mate of a male (billy) goat.

clue.text: Where strikers should be, honest!

explanation.surface: A football coach insists the forwards play forward and be straight with him.
explanation.walkthrough: Strikers are attacking footballers, who play in the forward line; the second sense is candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Forwards play at the front of the team, and the phrase also means frank and open.

clue.text: Outshine, yet it reduces the light

explanation.surface: Something outshines, yet dims, the light.
explanation.walkthrough: As a verb it means surpass; as a noun it is the sun or moon being blocked.
explanation.definitionFit: To outshine is to surpass, and in astronomy one body blocking another cuts off sunlight or moonlight.

clue.text: Dogs heard in the mountains

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for the dogs is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: pekes are Pekingese dogs

explanation.surface: Dogs are heard barking in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Summits or tops of hills stand for the mountains in general.

clue.text: Model accepts the French will make a scene

indicators.note: model as a verb, to shape, says the letters of accepts are re-formed

parts.note: le is the French masculine for the

explanation.surface: A model agrees that French designers will make a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a noun doing the accepting, but it is the anagram signal on ACCEPTS, giving SPECTAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacular public display is a scene, as in 'making a scene'.

clue.text: Carelessly I filled in very large areas of Texas

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the abbreviation for very large

parts.note: OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize

indicators.note: carelessly means the letters of I filled are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone carelessly filled in huge stretches of Texas.
explanation.walkthrough: OS for outsize is a clothing-size label; 'Carelessly' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Texas is known for its petroleum-producing land, the regions where crude is extracted.

clue.text: It's Royal Duke! Rest col- G lapse after Canal Turn

indicators.note: after puts the collapsed rest behind the turned canal
turn means the letters of canal are twisted round
collapse means the letters of rest fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A royal duke watches horses fall after the Canal Turn fence in a steeplechase.
explanation.walkthrough: Canal Turn is a famous fence at Aintree racecourse. 'Turn' rearranges CANAL into LANCA, 'collapse' rearranges REST into STER.
explanation.definitionFit: The reigning British monarch holds the title Duke of Lancaster, so it is a royal dukedom.

clue.text: Minimal fashions, at any rate

parts.note: minimal means the least
fashions in the sense of manners or methods: ways

explanation.surface: At any rate, minimalist fashions are in.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial adverb meaning at least or anyhow, a hedge in speech.

clue.text: Silver goes after gold in his work

definitions.text: Silver goes after gold in his work

parts.words: Silver goes after gold in his work
parts.note: silver is a pirate character hunting buried gold in a famous adventure novel, so the clue describes its author

explanation.surface: An Olympic ranking: silver comes after gold.
explanation.walkthrough: Long John Silver hunts for gold in Treasure Island, written by the Scottish novelist Robert Louis Stevenson.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish author whose pirate novel features a one-legged buccaneer seeking treasure.

clue.text: Warriors from Asia sadly take up drink

indicators.note: take means the jumbled letters hold the drink inside them
sadly means the letters of Asia are put into a wretched new order
up in a down clue says the word for drink is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: Warriors from Asia sadly turn to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take up' does two jobs in one phrase: 'take' holds one piece inside the other and 'up' reverses the drink, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The hereditary military class of feudal Japan, its fighting men.

clue.text: Old lover was awfully trendy

indicators.note: awfully means the letters of was are badly arranged

parts.note: in means fashionable

explanation.surface: An ex-boyfriend was terribly fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges WAS into SWA.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic, dated word for a young suitor or beau.

clue.text: Butterflies emerge when Severn is diverted

indicators.note: is diverted pictures the river's course rerouted, so the letters of Severn are reordered

explanation.surface: Butterflies appear when the River Severn changes course.
explanation.walkthrough: The Severn is Britain's longest river; 'is diverted' rearranges its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterflies in the stomach is the jittery feeling of anxiety before an ordeal.

clue.text: Deserved to hold ceremony in holiday destination

indicators.note: to hold means the holiday destination contains the ceremony

parts.note: the Med, the Mediterranean, is a popular holiday destination
a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: A couple deserved to have their wedding somewhere sunny.
explanation.definitionFit: Earned or warranted, as a reward that was fully justified.

clue.text: Studies origins of Roman Empire, another dull subject

indicators.note: origins of means the first letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A student complains that the Roman Empire is yet another dull subject.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of Roman Empire Another Dull Subject spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To study a subject at a British university is to read it.

clue.text: Right to interrupt stupid plan

indicators.note: to interrupt means the letter for right breaks into the word for stupid

parts.note: daft is British slang for stupid

explanation.surface: Someone's right to object to a foolish scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A preliminary outline or version of a scheme or document.

clue.text: Financial expert wants German car, mostly blue

parts.note: Audi is a German car make

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: blue is the colour of the Conservatives, so a blue is a Tory

explanation.surface: An accountant wants a German car, mostly in blue.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics blue is the Conservative colour, so 'blue' is TORY, cut to TOR by 'mostly'.
explanation.definitionFit: An accountant who checks a firm's books officially is a money expert.

clue.text: Some did it together just the same

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people did it together, and in just the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto means as before, the same thing again.

clue.text: Driving schools teach this way, with skill

parts.note: a way is a road
craft means skill

explanation.surface: Driving instructors teach this method, with skill.
explanation.definitionFit: The skill of handling a vehicle safely on the highway, taught to learner motorists.

clue.text: Article about another Macbeth, for example

indicators.note: about means the first article goes round the second

parts.note: the is the definite article
another article, here the indefinite an

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about yet another production of the Scottish play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means a second article: AN, which THE goes 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth held the rank of a Scottish nobleman, Thane of Glamis and then Cawdor.

clue.text: He investigates what turns persons to crime

indicators.note: turns means the letters of persons to crime are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A question of what drives people to commit offences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' rearranges PERSONS TO CRIME; Colin Dexter's Oxford detective, known from British television.
explanation.definitionFit: Colin Dexter's fictional Oxford police detective, who solves murders.
